title: Implement documentation criticality registry and journey gates
outOfScope: Rewriting or translating P0 product content, localized documentation homes, or README journeys.
Requiring complete Japanese or Simplified Chinese parity for P1 or P2 documents.
Changing runtime behavior, release logic, or unrelated governance checks.
Publishing, pushing, opening, or merging the Work Item branch.

sources.reason: Approved reader-first documentation governance design, P0/P1/P2 policy, and migration semantics.
Test-first WI-1 implementation plan and exact file/task boundaries.
Existing authority registry to extend without creating a competing source of truth.
Existing v1 agent documentation authority validator and read-set query.
Existing public documentation metadata gate for integration.
Existing authority behavior tests that must remain compatible.
Current page roles and multilingual architecture documentation.

riskAssessment.reason: The change adds policy validation and tests across documentation governance surfaces; missing-locale or link-graph false positives could block future documentation work.

reasons: Medium-risk governance policy change with deterministic tests and no runtime product behavior change.

executionDecision.reason: The user explicitly authorized execution of the accepted documentation plan and requested that the authorization be recorded in the Contract.

rawUserRequest: 查收，执行计划。我授权给你，并写入Contract。
preReviewWarnings: Check that planned P0 gaps are visible but do not masquerade as passing multilingual coverage.
Check that v1 agent read-set behavior remains unchanged while v2 reader-topic policy is added.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: Authority registry v2 accepts v1 compatibility records and declares reader topics without changing the default agent read set.
P0/P1/P2 topic validation enforces criticality, locale, ownership, active/planned migration status, and visible planned gaps.
Localized journey validation checks P0 reachability, same-language routes, explicit P1 English fallback labels, and historical-route exclusion.
The public documentation metadata gate and a focused Make target run the new validation.
Focused positive and negative tests cover schema compatibility, migration safety, link graphs, and aggregate gate integration.
Maintainer documentation explains the authority-versus-criticality boundary without claiming P0 migration is complete.
guidelines: Keep the existing v1 agent documentation read-set output backward compatible.
Use pure standard-library validation functions with deterministic, path-qualified errors.
Do not weaken active P0 topics back to planned.
Document new public Make and Python entrypoints.
Do not import internal modules from unrelated features.

intent.problem: Important documentation is currently governed mainly by file metadata and bounded translation checks, not by reader-criticality or complete same-language journeys. The initiative needs an executable registry and navigation policy before content migration can be safely staged.
constraints: Extend the existing authority registry; do not create a competing registry.
Keep v1 agent read-set behavior compatible.
Planned P0 gaps are visible but non-blocking until a topic becomes active; active topics cannot be downgraded.
This Work Item does not rewrite or translate product content.
Use standard-library code and existing Make/pytest conventions.
intent.rationale: A machine-readable criticality and journey policy gives later content Work Items a deterministic contract for what must be translated, linked, and reviewed.

scenarioCoverage.expected: The localized journey gate fails with a path-qualified error.
